final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and explicitly conceded the core unresolved facts: the affected use case remains exposed, approved risk acceptance is absent, disclosure is still required, and rollout controls alone do not satisfy the policy condition. That narrows the claim, but it does not convert the record into compliance. A monitored, reversible launch may be operationally bounded, yet the governing policy states that mitigation is sufficient only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. On the admissible record, neither condition is met. This is therefore not merely a documentation caveat that can support compliant_with_caveats; it is an unresolved compliance predicate, so noncompliant remains the proportional outcome.
remaining_concerns: The affected energy outage response use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
No approved risk acceptance covering that exposed segment is in the admissible record.
The policy text makes exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance a predicate for mitigation of a material model-card weakness.
Rollout controls, monitoring, rollback, and a 9% initial cohort support operational caution but do not satisfy the unresolved policy condition.
Disclosure is required on the current record, but disclosure alone does not cure the unmet compliance predicate for exposed material weakness.
